target_customer: Small and regional airlines, mostly in emerging markets, that pay for a passenger service system
problem: Small airlines run on legacy reservation systems, custom software or manual tools such as email and spreadsheets, and enterprise vendors serve them poorly.
business_model: Software platform priced per passenger flown (per profile sites, unverified)
product_category: Airline operating system and passenger service system

founders.name: Askhat Omarov
previous_startups: Asia InterCommunications (systems integrator in Kazakhstan, large Cisco partner there)
Santufei.com (online travel agency founded 2015, acquired by Kaspi.kz in 2020)
founders.background_notes: Per Sturgeon Capital article (March 2025). Education not stated in sources opened. YC page lists him as the only founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: A full airline reservation, inventory and departure control stack must be certified and integrated with distribution and payments, which is heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Once an airline migrates its inventory, reservations and check-in, switching is costly and slow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Farel; the Sturgeon article describes Amadeus as enterprise focused and underserving small airlines.

market_need_then: Sturgeon Capital describes over 1,000 small airlines in emerging markets with about 20 percent of global passenger volume, many on legacy or manual systems. The 2020 pandemic pushed airlines to cut costs; no 2020 dated source was opened.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, claims full control versus legacy PSS vendors

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B brand known to airline buyers; no press on the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Farel is active with a small team and live airline customers across four continents per its site. Funding is modest, a seed from Sturgeon, SNR and Bloomberg Beta with a reported 4.5M figure. The founder had sold a travel startup, which helps with credibility. The outcome is still open: airline software sales cycles are long and the market of small carriers is limited.
notes: Sturgeon says its seed investment was made in Q1 2023 with undisclosed size; an aggregator reports a 4.5M seed in January 2025 and CB Insights lists a 130K total; these may be the same or different rounds and conflict. Competitor search found only 2025 or undated vendor pages (Radixx, IBS, Hitit, Amadeus), so the list is empty because no source dated near the 2020 batch was found.
